name: Simon
source_summary: A Samaritan sorcerer who professed belief and was baptized under Philip's ministry, but was sharply rebuked by Peter after trying to buy the Holy Spirit's power with money.
family_friendly_summary: Simon was a sorcerer in Samaria who had amazed the local people for a long time with his magic, to the point that people called him "the Great Power of God." When Philip came preaching about Jesus and performing genuine miracles, Simon himself believed, was baptized, and started following Philip closely, astonished by what he saw. Later, when the apostles Peter and John came and prayed for believers in Samaria to receive the Holy Spirit, Simon saw this happen and offered the apostles money, asking them to give him the same power to pass on the Spirit to others. Peter rebuked him sharply, telling him his heart was not right before God and that he needed to repent of his wicked intent. Simon's story is a warning about seeking spiritual power for the wrong reasons -- for personal gain and prestige rather than genuine faith.
adult_story: Simon practiced sorcery in Samaria and had amazed the population for a long time, so that people called him "the Great Power of God" (Acts 8:9-11). When Philip came preaching Christ and performing genuine signs, Simon himself believed and was baptized, and "continued on with Philip" astonished at the miracles he witnessed (8:12-13). When the apostles Peter and John arrived from Jerusalem and laid hands on the new believers so they received the Holy Spirit, Simon saw the visible result and offered the apostles money, asking, "give this authority to me as well, so that everyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit" (8:14-19) -- treating a gift of God's Spirit as a marketable power he could purchase and resell for his own prestige. Peter's rebuke was severe and direct: "may your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money... your heart is not right before God" (8:20-21). He called Simon to repent and pray for forgiveness, warning he was "in the gall of bitterness and in the bondage of iniquity" (8:22-23). Simon's response -- asking Peter to pray for him so that nothing Peter had said would happen to him -- leaves his final spiritual state genuinely ambiguous in the text (8:24). His name later gave rise to the term "simony," the sin of buying or selling spiritual office or power, a lasting warning against treating God's gifts as commodities.

devotionals: Simon believed the Holy Spirit's power could be bought with money. Salvation and every gift of grace come freely through Jesus, never something we can purchase or earn.
Peter told Simon his heart was not right before God, and called him to repent. Jesus welcomes that same honest repentance from anyone, however far they've drifted.
